planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown clumps in spring in full sun and moist, well-drained soil.

directions: German-bred and more compact than many maiden grass selections, 'Ferner Osten' forms a tidy fountain of narrow green leaves with a fine central white rib that gives the clump a light, airy movement. Deep red plumes open above the foliage in late summer, aging to pink and then silver as they persist into winter, and the leaf blades turn a coppery orange in fall. Choose this cultivar over larger Miscanthus selections where a smaller footprint is needed but the same feathery winter interest is still wanted. Cut the whole clump back to a few inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun; established clumps tolerate both dry and periodically wet soil.

directions: One of the older red-tinged switchgrass selections, 'Hanse Herms' forms a narrow, upright clump of steel-blue foliage that reddens progressively through summer until it is a deep burgundy by fall. A cloud of fine pink-tinted flower panicles hovers above the foliage in late summer, and the colored blades remain attractive well into winter. Gardeners choose it over green-leaved switchgrass cultivars specifically for this season-long color shift from blue to wine-red. It tolerates heat, drought, and occasional wet soil once established, making it a low-fuss vertical accent or screen.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and average, well-drained soil.

directions: Named for the German word for deer-brown, 'Rehbraun' is a compact, narrow-clumping switchgrass whose medium-green summer foliage shifts to a warm reddish-brown by late summer and holds that color into fall. Airy, purple-green flower panicles rise just above the foliage from midsummer through early autumn, giving the clump a hazy, cloud-like outline. It stays more upright and shorter than many switchgrass cultivars, so it works well toward the front of a border rather than as a tall screen. Once established it needs little care beyond cutting the dried clump back in late winter.

planting.note: Plant divisions or transplants in spring in full sun and lean, well-drained soil; avoid rich or heavily amended beds.

directions: Introduced by Jelitto Perennial Seeds, 'Prairie Blues' is a taller, more uniformly silver-blue selection of the native little bluestem, standing out from wild seed-grown plants that vary in color. The steel-blue summer foliage shifts to rosy orange and copper in fall, topped by fluffy silver seed heads that catch low autumn light. Gardeners pick this cultivar over straight-species little bluestem when they want dependable, consistent blue color across every plant in a mass planting. It thrives in poor, dry soil and needs no fertilizing or staking, only a late-winter cutback before new growth starts.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun to part shade and moist, well-drained soil; this hybrid is sterile and increased only by division.

directions: 'Waldenbuch' is a looser, more arching alternative to the ubiquitous 'Karl Foerster' feather reed grass, forming a tight clump of deep green foliage beneath softly nodding flower stems. The plumes emerge silvery green in midsummer and mature to a golden tan, standing well into winter before they shatter, while the foliage turns light yellow in fall. Choose this cultivar where a slightly more relaxed, less rigid silhouette is wanted than the stiffly vertical 'Karl Foerster'. It tolerates heavy clay and part shade better than many ornamental grasses, and needs only a hard cutback in late winter.

planting.note: Plant divisions or transplants in spring in full sun and hot, dry, well-drained soil; avoid wet winter sites.

directions: This selection of pink muhly grass was chosen specifically for flowering roughly three weeks earlier than the straight species, so the trademark haze of cotton-candy-pink plumes appears in late summer rather than fall, extending the display before cool weather arrives. Fine, wiry blue-green foliage forms a tidy mound that stays neat all season and needs no staking or deadheading. Gardeners in regions with shorter autumns choose 'Fast Forward' over standard pink muhly so the bloom show has time to develop before frost cuts it short. It thrives in hot, lean, well-drained soil and resents winter wet, so raised beds or sandy sites suit it best.
